cleanIntro: One book covers the whole Shadow Systems pistol line and it names your XR920 on its optic-fit tables, but two of its chapters are scoped to particular models — read the headings before you follow them. The field strip itself is common: unload, close the action, press the trigger, ease the slide back a sixteenth of an inch, drop both sides of the slide lock, and run the slide off the front. Four pieces and no tools. Shadow Systems then stops and says further disassembly belongs to an armorer, and this guide stops where the manual does.

steps.title: Magazine out, chamber checked twice
steps.action: Point the XR920 in a safe direction with your finger clear of the trigger guard, press the magazine release and pull the magazine out. Then push up on the slide release lever while drawing the slide back with your other hand so it locks open, and look into both the chamber and the magazine well. Shadow Systems asks you to inspect both places, not one, because a round that has slipped out of a magazine can sit in the well and feed itself the moment a fresh magazine goes in.
steps.prose: This is a striker gun with no manual safety. The chamber check is the only thing standing between you and a discharge during the takedown pull.
steps.quote: Once the slide is locked to the rear, thoroughly inspect the chamber and the magazine well of the pistol to be sure that no ammunition remains in either place.
steps.cite: SAFTEY & OPERATION MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision or edition statement is printed anywhere in the document. The published filename carries '_updated-10-22' but that is a filename, not a printed edition, and is not treated as one. — Disassembly, p.23
steps.warn: The pistol will fire with the magazine out if a round is left in the chamber.

steps.title: Which XR920 you have decides which sections apply
steps.action: Two sections of this book are scoped to particular models and the XR920 is inside both. The interchangeable backstrap and magwell system is headed for DR, XR and MR models only, so it applies to you; the optic mounting section applies only if your slide is optic-ready. Look for the recessed optic cut in the slide before following that chapter.
steps.prose: The optic-fit table that covers you is the one headed MR920 / MR920L / XR920 / DR920 / DR920P. The CR920's table is separate and its spacer and screw counts differ.
steps.caution: The compensator chapters at the back are DR920P only and are not an XR920 procedure.
steps.quote:
Backstrap and Magwell Features
(DR, XR, MR Models ONLY)
steps.cite: SAFTEY & OPERATION MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision or edition statement is printed anywhere in the document. The published filename carries '_updated-10-22' but that is a filename, not a printed edition, and is not treated as one. — Backstrap and Magwell Features, p.12

steps.title: Close the action and press the trigger
steps.action: With the pistol empty and pointed somewhere safe, run the slide back and let it close on the empty chamber, then press the trigger. You will feel the striker release and hear the firing pin move forward. The XR920 cannot be stripped with the striker cocked — the slide lock will not clear the striker's bearing surface — so this is not an optional courtesy step, it is part of the mechanism.
steps.prose: Do this deliberately and consciously, with the muzzle in a safe direction. Every negligent discharge during a Glock-pattern takedown happens at exactly this moment, on a gun the owner was certain was empty.
steps.quote: Point the pistol in a safe direction, and then pull the trigger.  You will hear the firing pin move forward.
steps.cite: SAFTEY & OPERATION MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision or edition statement is printed anywhere in the document. The published filename carries '_updated-10-22' but that is a filename, not a printed edition, and is not treated as one. — Disassembly, p.24
steps.warn: Muzzle in a safe direction before the trigger is touched.

steps.title: One sixteenth of an inch, no more
steps.action: Grip the top of the slide with the fingers of one hand and draw it back about a sixteenth of an inch — a movement you feel rather than see. Simultaneously pull down and hold both sides of the slide lock with the thumb and index finger of your free hand. Pull the slide back further than that sixteenth and you reset the trigger, which locks the slide lock and stops the strip dead.
steps.prose: Both sides of the slide lock have to come down together. Pressing only the side you can see leaves the far end still engaged, and it feels exactly like a stuck slide.
steps.caution: Both sides together. One side alone will not release it.
steps.quote: Simultaneously, pull down and hold both sides of the slide lock using the thumb and index finger of your free hand.
steps.cite: SAFTEY & OPERATION MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision or edition statement is printed anywhere in the document. The published filename carries '_updated-10-22' but that is a filename, not a printed edition, and is not treated as one. — Disassembly, p.24

steps.title: Slide forward off the frame
steps.action: Keep the slide lock down and push the slide forward until it comes fully off the front of the receiver. It should run off smoothly. If it hangs up part way, you have almost certainly reset the trigger by over-travelling in the last step — Shadow Systems' own remedy is to pull the trigger a second time and try again, and if it still fights you, start the sequence over.
steps.prose: Do not force it. The slide is running on its rails and a hang-up is always the striker or the lock, never friction.
steps.aside: The receiver stays assembled. Everything else comes out of the slide.
steps.quote: NOTE: Occasionally, users will accidentally reset the trigger by pulling the slide back too far in step 4.  If you find the slide “hangs up” as you are trying to remove it, pull the trigger a second time and it should move freely off the receiver.
steps.cite: SAFTEY & OPERATION MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision or edition statement is printed anywhere in the document. The published filename carries '_updated-10-22' but that is a filename, not a printed edition, and is not treated as one. — Disassembly, p.24

steps.title: Recoil spring assembly out
steps.action: Turn the slide upside down. Push the recoil spring assembly slightly forward against its own tension to unseat the rear end from the barrel lug, then lift it away and out. It comes out as one captive unit — do not try to separate the rod from the spring.
steps.prose: The forward push is small and the spring is stiff. Keep a thumb over it so it does not launch when it clears the lug.
steps.caution: The assembly is under tension until it is clear of the barrel lug.
steps.quote: Push the recoil spring assembly slightly forward while lifting it away from the barrel.
steps.cite: SAFTEY & OPERATION MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision or edition statement is printed anywhere in the document. The published filename carries '_updated-10-22' but that is a filename, not a printed edition, and is not treated as one. — Disassembly, p.25

steps.title: Barrel out of the slide
steps.action: With the spring out, lift the barrel up and back out of the slide. Nothing holds it in but the locking block cutout, so it lifts free with no resistance at all. That is the whole field strip: frame, slide, barrel, recoil spring assembly.
steps.prose: Four pieces, no tools. Anything beyond this is armorer work.
steps.quote: Lift the barrel from the slide.
steps.cite: SAFTEY & OPERATION MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision or edition statement is printed anywhere in the document. The published filename carries '_updated-10-22' but that is a filename, not a printed edition, and is not treated as one. — Disassembly, p.25

steps.title: Bore from the chamber end
steps.action: With the barrel out, run a bore brush wet with solvent through it from the chamber end forward, then patches until they come out clean. Working chamber-to-muzzle keeps fouling moving the way the bullet went and keeps the brush off the crown. Standard firearm solvents are fine on this pistol; what is not fine is leaving them pooled inside it.
steps.prose: Excess solvent left in the gun collects dirt and can creep into primers on the next loaded round.
steps.caution: Do not leave excess solvent inside the pistol.
steps.quote: Barrel: Once field stripped, the barrel and chamber are easily cleaned from the chamber end using a bore brush, patches, and solvent.
steps.cite: SAFTEY & OPERATION MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision or edition statement is printed anywhere in the document. The published filename carries '_updated-10-22' but that is a filename, not a printed edition, and is not treated as one. — Cleaning, p.26

steps.title: Breech face and under the extractor claw — dry
steps.action: Work a toothbrush-type tool into the slide's rail cuts with a clean patch, then get into the breech face and under the extractor claw. Those two spots must finish absolutely dry and free of debris. Carbon packed behind an extractor claw is the single most common cause of a Glock-pattern gun failing to eject, and oil there simply glues the next lot of carbon in place.
steps.prose: Dry means dry. This is the one area on the slide that gets no lubricant at all.
steps.quote: The breech face and the area under the extractor claw should be cleaned with a toothbrush-type cleaning tool and be absolutely dry and free of any dirt and debris after cleaning.
steps.cite: SAFTEY & OPERATION MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision or edition statement is printed anywhere in the document. The published filename carries '_updated-10-22' but that is a filename, not a printed edition, and is not treated as one. — Cleaning, p.26
steps.warn: Never oil the breech face or the extractor claw.

steps.title: Oil the rails, oil the connector, oil nothing else
steps.action: Wipe the outside of the barrel including the hood and lugs, the inside top of the slide where the hood rubs, and the muzzle opening with a lightly oiled patch. Then put one drop of oil the length of each slide rail cut, and one drop where the rear of the trigger bar meets the connector at the right rear corner of the frame. That is the complete lubrication schedule — more oil is not better on this gun.
steps.prose: The trigger bar and connector are what you feel in the trigger. A dry corner there is what turns a clean break gritty.
steps.quote: A drop of oil is needed where the rear end of the trigger bar touches the connector at the right rear corner of the frame.
steps.cite: SAFTEY & OPERATION MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision or edition statement is printed anywhere in the document. The published filename carries '_updated-10-22' but that is a filename, not a printed edition, and is not treated as one. — Lubrication, p.27
steps.warn: Warning: Do not put oil or solvent inside of the firing pin channel it can cause contamination of primers and failure to fire.

steps.title: Stop where the manual stops
steps.action: Do not take the slide or the frame down any further. Shadow Systems states outright that further disassembly is neither required nor recommended and belongs to a certified gunsmith or armorer. The striker channel in particular must stay dry and untouched — it is not a user-serviceable area on this pistol.
steps.prose: The field strip reaches everything that fouls. What is left behind the breech face is sealed for a reason.
steps.quote: Further disassembly by the user is neither required nor recommended and should only be performed by certified gunsmiths or armorers.
steps.cite: SAFTEY & OPERATION MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision or edition statement is printed anywhere in the document. The published filename carries '_updated-10-22' but that is a filename, not a printed edition, and is not treated as one. — Disassembly, p.26

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: You are down to four pieces: receiver, slide, barrel, recoil spring assembly. That is the whole of the field strip Shadow Systems publishes for the XR920, and the manual draws the line immediately after it. Beyond this the manual sends you to an armorer, so there is no Deep Clean to walk.
steps.prose: Clean it, lubricate it to the two-drop schedule, and put it back together by reversing the order.
steps.quote: Further disassembly by the user is neither required nor recommended and should only be performed by certified gunsmiths or armorers.
steps.cite: SAFTEY & OPERATION MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision or edition statement is printed anywhere in the document. The published filename carries '_updated-10-22' but that is a filename, not a printed edition, and is not treated as one. — Disassembly, p.26

deepAbsentReason: Shadow Systems publishes NO deeper procedure for this pistol. The manual stops at the field strip and states in its own words that further disassembly is neither required nor recommended and should only be performed by certified gunsmiths or armorers (Disassembly, p.26). The only teardown beyond the field strip anywhere in the book is the DR920P compensator, and that chapter is scoped by the manual itself to integrally compensated pistols. There is nothing published to walk, and inventing a striker-channel or frame teardown for it would be substitution.

cleaning.name: BARREL
tasks: Brush and patch the bore from the CHAMBER end forward until patches come out clean
Wipe the barrel exterior, the hood and the locking lugs with a lightly oiled patch
Do not leave excess solvent standing inside the barrel or the slide

cleaning.name: SLIDE
tasks: Clean the rail cuts with a clean patch on a toothbrush-type tool
Clean the breech face and under the extractor claw and leave both ABSOLUTELY DRY
Wipe every other exposed area of the slide clean
Oil the inside top of the slide forward of the ejection port where the barrel hood rubs
One drop of oil along the full length of each slide rail cut

cleaning.name: FRAME
tasks: Wipe exposed frame parts with a cloth slightly dampened with solvent, then wipe them dry
One drop of oil where the rear of the trigger bar meets the connector at the right rear corner
NEVER put oil or solvent in the firing pin channel
Check no cotton, threads or patch debris are left in the action before reassembly

cleaning.name: MAGAZINES
tasks: Keep magazines clean and in good repair — magazine faults are the number one cause of malfunctions
Wipe the follower and the feed lips; do not oil the inside of the magazine body

reassembly: Drop the barrel back into the slide, then push the recoil spring assembly forward and seat its rear end against the barrel lug.
Set the slide on the receiver rails and pull it fully to the rear. That rearward pull is what completes the reassembly.
If the slide hangs up going on, the guide rod is not fully seated and centred against the barrel — check it before forcing anything.
A slight downward pull on the takedown lever also helps if the slide binds during reassembly.
Function check the trigger and the slide lock on the empty gun before a magazine goes anywhere near it.
fncheck: With the pistol empty, rack the slide and let it slam forward under its own spring — do not ride it. Press the trigger and confirm it breaks and resets when the slide is cycled. Lock the slide back on an empty magazine and confirm the slide release drops it. If the slide hangs up during reassembly, the recoil spring guide rod is not fully seated and centred against the barrel; seat it and try again rather than forcing the slide on.
